newsitem.title: UK: UK unions notify Barclays of overtime ban.
newsitem.headline: UK unions notify Barclays of overtime ban.

text.p: Barclays Plc, the British banking giant, faces industrial action by staff from August 21, one of the unions representing banking and finance workers said on Wednesday.

"Barclays Bank are today being given formal notice by finance union BIFU and Barclays union UNiFI of the unions' intention to start an overtime ban," the Banking Insurance and Finance Union (BIFU) said.
Pay negotiations between the unions and Barclays broke down last week. BIFU says the pay proposals "leave 25,000 staff facing a pay freeze".

BIFU said in a statement that Barclays, which last week announced pre-tax profits for the first half of the year of 1.376 billion pounds, had refused a request to refer the dispute to government industrial relations arbitration service ACAS.

"As (Barclay's chairman) Andrew Buxton said...the main driver of the profit growth has been the UK bank," BIFU negotiator Jennifer Cole said. "The average return on shareholders funds was 24.4 percent, yet 25,000 of their staff face a pay freeze," she added.

BIFU said the unions expected the overtime ban, which will come into force from 0001 BST on Thursday 21 August, to cause severe disruption and delays to customer accounts and transactions. Cash machines are also likely to be affected, it said.
